newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary govt sends proposal to protesting farmers.
newsitem.headline: Hungary govt sends proposal to protesting farmers.

text.p: The Hungarian government sent a proposed agreement on Thursday to farmers who have been protesting over tax changes by blockading roads, a government spokesman said.
"The letter should reach them by the deadline (of 1700 GMT)," government spokesman Elemer Kiss told a news conference following the weekly cabinet meeting.

He said the government had agreed with the farmers on several points, such as modifying tax and social security rules and reducing paperwork. Agreement was not reached on some other issues, but Kiss said the government was not prepared to give more.
The farmers have blocked roads throughout the country with tractors, ploughs, harvesters and other equipment since Monday.
They are protesting at the end of an exemption from social security contributions as of January 1 and new requirements to provide documentation for tax purposes.

On Tuesday, representatives of the government and the farmers reached an agreement over most of the issues and this is what the letter -- signed by Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy, contains -- Kiss said.
The farmers said on Tuesday that if they received the government's written proposals by 1700 GMT on Thursday, they will answer them by the same hour on Friday.
However, due to the fact that different farmers' organisations have announced a series of protests some roadblocks could remain even after a Friday agreement.

The Peasants' Association did not yet call off a March 10 protest for raising the tax-free income treshhold to one million forints per year despite the fact that the cabinet's proposal already raised it to 1.5 million.
On Thursday, only a fraction of Wednesday's 74 raod blocks were in place, causing little disruption in traffic.
